questions.q: Why should you start a reproduction attempt from the authors' released code rather than your own reimplementation?
options: Released code is always bug-free
The code is the ground truth of what was actually run, while the paper is a lossy summary of it
Reimplementing from scratch is against journal policy
It's faster to write a reimplementation than to clone a repository
questions.explain: The paper's prose can omit details that only the code reveals, so starting from the official code first tells you what was actually run before you introduce your own implementation choices.

questions.q: Why is debugging your own reimplementation directly against the paper's reported number considered backwards?
options: It isn't backwards — it's the recommended first step
You can't tell whether a gap is a bug in your code or a real discrepancy, since you have no working baseline to compare against
Papers never report accurate numbers
Reimplementations always outperform the original code
questions.explain: Without first confirming the official code reproduces the reported number, you have no way to isolate whether a gap in your reimplementation is your own bug or a genuine discrepancy.

questions.q: What does pinning a random seed and disabling nondeterministic cuDNN kernels actually guarantee?
options: Bit-identical results across any GPU model or library version
Removal of one axis of run-to-run variation, though not a guarantee of identical results across different hardware
That the reproduction will exactly match the paper's reported number
Nothing useful for reproducibility
questions.explain: Seeding and deterministic settings remove one source of variation within your own attempt, but hardware and library differences can still cause numerical differences across environments.

questions.q: What is a 'qualitative trend match' as described in this lesson?
options: An exact numerical match within the expected noise band
The direction and rough shape of a result holding even though the absolute numbers differ, often due to a smaller compute budget
A match verified only by visual inspection of a figure
Any result that beats the original paper's number
questions.explain: A qualitative trend match is a weaker, but still informative, standard where the relative conclusion (e.g., method A beats method B) holds even if exact numbers don't match, typically because of reduced compute.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize matching hyperparameters exactly rather than approximately?
options: Because 'approximately the same settings' doesn't constitute a reproduction and can introduce unaccounted-for differences
Exact hyperparameters are always listed in the abstract
Approximate settings are forbidden by most ML conferences
Hyperparameters never affect training outcomes
questions.explain: Settings like optimizer betas, learning rate schedule, and warmup can meaningfully change outcomes, so matching them exactly (using the code's values when the paper omits them) is necessary for a real reproduction attempt.
